name: LMF (lactate mineral medium supplemented with sodium fumarate) (PMC7253198)
description: LMF (lactate mineral medium supplemented with sodium fumarate) — medium reported in PMC7253198 (complex/undefined base — extracts not BiGG-mappable).

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC7253198 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Complex medium: chemically-defined portion mapped to BiGG; biological extracts listed in `unmapped`. Added via GrowthDB curation.
provenance.verification: paper-verified (complete recipe; cited + supplementary sources chased)
provenance.verification_evidence: LM medium (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.5; 100 mM NaCl; 0.02% yeast extract; 0.01% peptone; 15 mM lactate) [Kreienbaum et al. 2020, PMC7530303]; 'lactate medium (LM): 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 200 mM NaCl, 0.02% (w/v) yeast extract, 0.01% (w/v) peptone, 15 mM lactate' [Rick et al. 2022, PMC9061725]
provenance.base_medium: LM medium (lactate medium) of the Thormann lab, cited by Stalder et al. as Paulick et al. 2009: 10 mM HEPES (pH 7.4-7.5), 100 mM NaCl (200 mM in some variants), 0.02% (w/v) yeast extract, 0.01% (w/v) peptone, 15 mM lactate.

sources_chased.what: base recipe cited as 'lactate mineral medium (Paulick et al. 2009)' = Paulick A, Koerdt A, Lassak J, Huntley S, Wilms I, Narberhaus F, Thormann KM. 2009. Two different stator systems drive a single polar flagellum in Shewanella oneidensis MR-1. Mol Microbiol 71(4):836. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2958.2008.06570.x
sources_chased.how: WebFetch of Wiley full text/PDF returned HTTP 403 (paywalled); recipe reconstructed from concordant restatements in Thormann-lab papers that cite Paulick 2009 for LM medium

sources_chased.what: LM medium verbatim recipe + Paulick attribution
sources_chased.how: WebFetch Kreienbaum et al. 2020 (PMC7530303), Rick et al. 2022 (PMC9061725), Binnenkade et al. 2018 (PMC6085458), Godeke et al. 2011 (PMC3105746) - all Thormann-lab papers citing 'LM medium (Paulick et al., 2009)'
added: confirmed LM medium = HEPES + NaCl + 0.02% yeast extract + 0.01% peptone + 15 mM lactate
confirmed Paulick 2009 is the defining reference

missing_before: HEPES buffer (10 mM) - the actual buffer (medium is NOT phosphate-buffered)
yeast extract (0.02% w/v) - undefined complex ingredient supplying N, P, S, K, Mg, Ca, trace metals and vitamins
recuration.notes: Despite being called 'lactate mineral medium' by Stalder et al., the Paulick 2009 'LM medium' is a HEPES-buffered lactate medium containing yeast extract + peptone as complex ingredients, NOT a fully defined mineral medium with a salts/trace-element stock. Nitrogen, phosphate, sulfate, K, Mg, Ca and all trace metals (Fe, Zn, Mn, Co, Cu) and vitamins are supplied by the 0.02% yeast extract + 0.01% peptone (which the DB decomposes separately), so the ion exchanges in the original component list are justified by these complex ingredients rather than by defined salts. yeast extract.citation: Yeast extract = autolysate of Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Component amounts here are QUANTITATIVE (mg per g yeast extract), from Tao Z et al., J Microbiol Biotechnol 2022;32:1236-1247, Table 2 (doi:10.4014/jmb.2207.07057, PMC9998214): free amino acids ~35% w/w with the measured pattern (Ala/Glu/Asp/Leu/Arg/Lys dominant; Cys/Met/Trp minor), B-vitamins (niacin >> pyridoxine/pantothenate > thiamine > riboflavin/folate/B12; biotin trace), ~10% RNA-derived nucleosides, and minerals (K/P-rich). Corroborated by Podpora B et al., Czech J Food Sci 2016;34:554-563, doi:10.17221/419/2015-CJFS; Atlas RM, Handbook of Microbiological Media, doi:10.1201/EBK1439804063. Per-component lower bounds are scaled to molar abundance (mg/g ÷ molecular weight).

components.decomposition_ref: Yeast extract = autolysate of Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Component amounts here are QUANTITATIVE (mg per g yeast extract), from Tao Z et al., J Microbiol Biotechnol 2022;32:1236-1247, Table 2 (doi:10.4014/jmb.2207.07057, PMC9998214): free amino acids ~35% w/w with the measured pattern (Ala/Glu/Asp/Leu/Arg/Lys dominant; Cys/Met/Trp minor), B-vitamins (niacin >> pyridoxine/pantothenate > thiamine > riboflavin/folate/B12; biotin trace), ~10% RNA-derived nucleosides, and minerals (K/P-rich). Corroborated by Podpora B et al., Czech J Food Sci 2016;34:554-563, doi:10.17221/419/2015-CJFS; Atlas RM, Handbook of Microbiological Media, doi:10.1201/EBK1439804063. Per-component lower bounds are scaled to molar abundance (mg/g ÷ molecular weight).
